What is the essential teaching in 'Navigating the New Millennium'?

In 'Navigating the New Millennium', the teaching opens with this observation: *"Although our calculation of time's passage in years and centuries carries no more weight against the vastness of the cosmic process than a feather before a storm, still, being human, it is natural for us to nurture hope on reaching the threshold of a new millennium."* The central invitation is to turn one's investigation inward — to verify the Dhamma not as a set of beliefs, but as directly observable reality in one's own body, speech, and mind. As the text teaches, the Dhamma is *akāliko* — ever-present — and *opanayiko* — leading inward — available to be known (*paccattaṁ*) by each practitioner for themselves. There is no need to search elsewhere; the truth is already here.

In this text, dukkha appears in this context: *"From one angle it could be said that what Buddhism can offer humankind today is exactly what it has been holding out for the past twenty-five centuries: an acute diagnosis of the human condition and a"* Understanding suffering (dukkha) is not merely conceptual — it is meant to be verified directly. The Dhamma is *ehipassiko*: 'come and see for yourself.' Bring the quality described by dukkha into direct investigation: where is it present in your current experience? When seen clearly, each of these Pāli terms dissolves from abstract concept into living reality.
